question_type: midpoint-normalized difference of one monthly ownership series between two month-ends; answer form disputed because a trailing units phrase ('billions of nominal dollars') contradicts a unitless metric (issue47)
decisive_step: Deciding the answer form: treat the metric noun phrase 'mid-point normalized difference' as fixing the quantity (difference divided by the mean of the two values, unscaled) and read 'reported in billions of nominal dollars' as describing the inputs, rather than dropping the normalization and reporting the raw dollar gap (or multiplying by 100). The reference made this call at worklog.md Step 1 (Ambiguity bullet) and Step 7 (Answer decision); review.md 'Findings' calls ratio-vs-percent the only residual ambiguity. Source selection is not load-bearing: OFS-1 column (7) and OFS-2 'Total privately held' give the same rounded ratio (worklog Step 6; calc.py cross-check), and neither June cell was ever revised (worklog Step 5).

It then weighed ratio vs percent vs raw gap (a[17], a[19], a[22]), grepped the corpus for the phrase (a[21], empty), and chose the unscaled ratio, quoting the AGENTS.md 'Percent or fraction' bullet to rule out x100 and reading 'billions' as the input unit (a[22]).

smallest_change.change: Rewrite the 'Percent or fraction' bullet as: 'Answer form: the metric named in the question fixes what you report. If it names a normalized difference, ratio, share, rate or percent change, report that metric, computed from the cited values, and never the raw difference of the inputs; a trailing phrase such as "in billions of nominal dollars" gives the unit of the inputs, not permission to drop the metric. Multiply by 100 only when the question says percent, percentage or %; a ratio, fraction, normalized difference or decimal is reported unscaled. Do not infer the scale from the rounding precision asked for.'
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely: a question that wants a raw difference in billions does not name a normalizing metric; the x100 clause is the existing bullet a already used at a[22]
smallest_change.confidence: medium (c had the current bullet and still chose the raw gap at T=1, but the current bullet says nothing about dropping the operator; b had no text at all; the question is on the disputed list, so validate on undisputed ratio questions)

notes: All three cells extracted the right two cells and printed the correct ratio in their own calc; the miss is purely the answer-form decision on a disputed question. Design points: (1) the current 'Percent or fraction' bullet covers x100 only; b and c failed on the other axis (dropping the operator), which the rewritten bullet names. (2) The OFS-1 vs OFS-2 detour (c[24]-c[33]) cannot change the rounded ratio; a sentence 'when two candidate series give the same rounded answer, stop comparing them' would save turns. (3) show_table's 'spurious extra label' NOTE fired correctly on OFS-2 in 2007_09 (c[26]), a good example of the label-independent anchor note that TSO Table 3 in 035 lacked. (4) show_table --grep is a plain substring: c wasted three calls on '\|' alternation here and 035 c[15] got a false hit on 'marketable'; either document it in the page footer or support OR.
